# Commands

Dispatch tasks to CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) in tmux windows and git worktrees. The same text is what `agentctl --help` and `agentctl <command> --help` print.

Options of every command: `-h, --help`. Options of `agentctl` itself: `-V, --version`.
Task IDs are case-insensitive and a unique prefix is enough for `attach`, `peek`, `hide`, `unhide`; the other commands take the full ID.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`new`](#agentctl-new) | Start the tasks in a spec file: worktree, setup commands, symlinks, TASK.md, tmux window, agent, prompt. |
| [`queue`](#agentctl-queue) | Put the tasks of a spec file in the queue: they start by themselves (while "agentctl watch" runs) when a window of their provider is free. Shows a summary and asks y/N first. |
| [`queue list`](#agentctl-queue-list) | The queue: position, task, agent/model/effort, priority, start condition and how long it waits. |
| [`queue rm`](#agentctl-queue-rm) | Take a task out of the queue (a waiting or a failed one). |
| [`queue up`](#agentctl-queue-up) | Move a waiting task to the front of the line (tasks with priority: high still go first). |
| [`queue retry`](#agentctl-queue-retry) | Put a failed task back at the end of the line; it is tried once more (over the worktree the failed start left). |
| [`queue pause`](#agentctl-queue-pause) | Stop starting queued tasks (running tasks are not touched; adding and listing still work). |
| [`queue resume`](#agentctl-queue-resume) | Let the queue start tasks again. |
| [`overlap`](#agentctl-overlap) | Which active tasks of one repository changed the same files (git diff of each worktree against its base, plus uncommitted files). Without a task: every pair. |
| [`send`](#agentctl-send) | Paste a follow-up prompt into the existing window of each task in the file. |
| [`status`](#agentctl-status) | Table of tasks: window state, running time, report, last output line. |
| [`archive`](#agentctl-archive) | Move the state of closed tasks (agentctl close) to the archive folder next to the state folder. Reports and worktrees are not touched. |
| [`hide`](#agentctl-hide) | Take tasks off the board and "status" (they stay in "status --all" and on the board under "a"). Does not close the task or touch its worktree. |
| [`unhide`](#agentctl-unhide) | Show hidden tasks again on the board and in "status". A task shown on purpose is not hidden again by board.auto_hide_pulled_dead. |
| [`pull`](#agentctl-pull) | Copy the task report to the clipboard and print its path (without a report: last 40 lines of the window). --ready: all new reports at once. |
| [`close`](#agentctl-close) | Kill the task windows; --rm-worktree also removes their git worktrees (branches are kept). Shows the list and asks y/N first. |
| [`watch`](#agentctl-watch) | Foreground loop: notifies (macOS notification / notify-send) when a task has a report ready, asks something, hit its usage limit, waits too long, needs folder trust or died. |
| [`board`](#agentctl-board) | Full-screen overview of the tasks: state, progress, a live preview of the selected window, and keys to switch to it, message, interrupt, pull and close. |
| [`notify-test`](#agentctl-notify-test) | Send one test notification and say which channel carried it (terminal-notifier with a click action, or the osascript fallback). |
| [`adopt`](#agentctl-adopt) | Restore the state file of a task whose TASK.md is lost (the report and the window are still there). Agent, model and effort default to "unknown". |
| [`interrupt`](#agentctl-interrupt) | Interrupt the task's current turn (sends the agent's interrupt key, default Escape); the window stays open. |
| [`attach`](#agentctl-attach) | Go to the task window: attach-session outside tmux, switch-client inside. Without a task: the only running one, or a list to choose from. |
| [`event`](#agentctl-event) | Called by the agents themselves (hooks that "new" sets up): records the event, updates the task state and notifies at once. Always exits 0. |
| [`move`](#agentctl-move) | Hand a task that hit its usage limit to the other provider: new window \<task>-2 in the same worktree, the original prompt plus a note to continue. Asks y/N. |
| [`peek`](#agentctl-peek) | Print the last lines of the task window (without the agent footer), to read along without attaching. |
| [`mcp`](#agentctl-mcp) | Local MCP server on stdio: lets a chat (the Claude app, Claude Code, VS Code) read status, window previews and reports. "mcp install" registers it; writing is off until mcp.allow says otherwise. |
| [`mcp serve`](#agentctl-mcp-serve) | Serve the tools on stdin/stdout (this is what the app or Claude Code starts). Nothing else is ever printed to stdout. |
| [`mcp install`](#agentctl-mcp-install) | Register this agentctl as an MCP server: --desktop edits claude_desktop_config.json (diff, y/N, dated .bak copy, other servers kept), --claude-code runs "claude mcp add --scope user". |
| [`mcp uninstall`](#agentctl-mcp-uninstall) | Remove the agentctl MCP server from the Claude desktop config and/or Claude Code (without a flag: both). |
| [`doctor`](#agentctl-doctor) | Check tmux, node, claude, codex, gh, the cache directory and the configs. |
| [`spec`](#agentctl-spec) | Spec helpers. |
| [`spec example`](#agentctl-spec-example) | Print an example spec (the Neon City example from the README). |

## agentctl new

Start the tasks in a spec file: worktree, setup commands, symlinks, TASK.md, tmux window, agent, prompt.

```
agentctl new [options] [file]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[file]` | spec file, or "-" for stdin |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, execute nothing |  |
| `--reuse` | use worktrees that already exist instead of failing |  |
| `--agent <agent>` | run every spec on this provider, translated through the equivalents table | one of `claude`, `codex` |
| `--no-switch` | never offer to move a task to the other provider when its limit is full |  |
| `--no-agent` | only create the worktree, run setup and links; no TASK.md, window or agent |  |
| `--no-wait-trust` | stop at the folder-trust dialog instead of waiting for you to confirm it (the old behaviour) |  |
| `--clip` | read the spec from the clipboard; shows a summary and asks y/N first |  |
| `-y, --yes` | with --clip: do not ask; also skips the question after a "touches" warning |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl new --dry-run nc-42.md        # print every command, run nothing
agentctl new nc-42.md                  # start the tasks of the file
agentctl new --clip                    # spec from the clipboard, summary, y/N
agentctl new --agent codex nc-42.md    # run the specs on Codex (models through the equivalents table)
agentctl new --no-agent nc-42.md       # only worktree, setup and links
```

## agentctl queue

Put the tasks of a spec file in the queue: they start by themselves (while "agentctl watch" runs) when a window of their provider is free. Shows a summary and asks y/N first.

Subcommands: `queue list`, `queue rm`, `queue up`, `queue retry`, `queue pause`, `queue resume`.

```
agentctl queue [options] [command] [file]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[file]` | spec file, or "-" for stdin |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--clip` | read the spec from the clipboard |  |
| `--agent <agent>` | run every spec on this provider, translated through the equivalents table (the queue never switches provider by itself) | one of `claude`, `codex` |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue nc-42.md                # summary, y/N, then the tasks wait for a free window
agentctl queue --clip -y               # spec from the clipboard, no question
agentctl queue --agent codex nc-42.md  # run them on Codex (through the equivalents table)
```

## agentctl queue list

The queue: position, task, agent/model/effort, priority, start condition and how long it waits.

```
agentctl queue list [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue list
agentctl queue list --json
```

## agentctl queue rm

Take a task out of the queue (a waiting or a failed one).

```
agentctl queue rm [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue rm NC-42
```

## agentctl queue up

Move a waiting task to the front of the line (tasks with priority: high still go first).

```
agentctl queue up [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue up NC-42                # first in line (priority: high still goes first)
```

## agentctl queue retry

Put a failed task back at the end of the line; it is tried once more (over the worktree the failed start left).

```
agentctl queue retry [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue retry NC-42             # after a failed start: back at the end of the line
```

## agentctl queue pause

Stop starting queued tasks (running tasks are not touched; adding and listing still work).

```
agentctl queue pause [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue pause                  # nothing new starts; running tasks are not touched
```

## agentctl queue resume

Let the queue start tasks again.

```
agentctl queue resume [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue resume
```

## agentctl overlap

Which active tasks of one repository changed the same files (git diff of each worktree against its base, plus uncommitted files). Without a task: every pair.

```
agentctl overlap [options] [task]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[task]` | only the pairs with this task; case does not matter and a unique prefix is enough |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl overlap                        # every pair of active tasks that changed the same files
agentctl overlap LANDING-QS-1           # only the pairs with this task
```

## agentctl send

Paste a follow-up prompt into the existing window of each task in the file.

```
agentctl send [options] [file]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[file]` | spec file (only "task" and the prompt are used), or "-" for stdin |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, execute nothing |  |
| `--clip` | read the prompt from the clipboard; shows a summary and asks y/N first |  |
| `-y, --yes` | with --clip: do not ask |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl send follow-up.md             # header: only "task:"; the prompt below it is pasted
agentctl send --clip -y                # follow-up from the clipboard, no question
```

## agentctl status

Table of tasks: window state, running time, report, last output line.

```
agentctl status [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |
| `--clip` | copy a compact Markdown table to the clipboard (to paste at the start of a chat session) |  |
| `--tmux-line` | one short line for the tmux status bar, like "2⚙ 1✓ 1? 3⧗" (tasks per state, then the tasks in the queue) |  |
| `--all` | also the hidden and the closed tasks (see "agentctl hide", "agentctl close"), archived ones included |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl status
agentctl status --json                 # rows with started (UTC) and startedLocal
agentctl status --clip                 # Markdown table to paste into a chat
agentctl status --all                  # hidden, closed and archived tasks too
```

## agentctl archive

Move the state of closed tasks (agentctl close) to the archive folder next to the state folder. Reports and worktrees are not touched.

```
agentctl archive [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--older-than <age>` | only tasks closed at least this long ago: 30m, 12h, 7d, 2w |  |
| `--dry-run` | print the moves, do nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl archive --older-than 7d --dry-run
```

## agentctl hide

Take tasks off the board and "status" (they stay in "status --all" and on the board under "a"). Does not close the task or touch its worktree.

```
agentctl hide [options] <tasks...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<tasks...>` | task IDs; case does not matter and a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl hide NC-41 NC-42
```

## agentctl unhide

Show hidden tasks again on the board and in "status". A task shown on purpose is not hidden again by board.auto_hide_pulled_dead.

```
agentctl unhide [options] <tasks...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<tasks...>` | task IDs; case does not matter and a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl unhide NC-42
```

## agentctl pull

Copy the task report to the clipboard and print its path (without a report: last 40 lines of the window). --ready: all new reports at once.

```
agentctl pull [options] [task]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[task]` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--ready` | join every report in state report-ready that was not pulled yet, copy it and mark the tasks as pulled |  |
| `--all` | with --ready: also the reports that were pulled before |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl pull NC-42                    # one report to the clipboard
agentctl pull --ready                    # all new reports in one text
agentctl pull --ready --all              # also the ones pulled before
```

## agentctl close

Kill the task windows; --rm-worktree also removes their git worktrees (branches are kept). Shows the list and asks y/N first.

```
agentctl close [options] <tasks...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<tasks...>` | task IDs |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--rm-worktree` | run "git worktree remove" for the task worktrees (never --force) |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, execute nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl close NC-41 NC-42 --rm-worktree
agentctl close NC-42 --dry-run
```

## agentctl watch

Foreground loop: notifies (macOS notification / notify-send) when a task has a report ready, asks something, hit its usage limit, waits too long, needs folder trust or died.

```
agentctl watch [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--tmux` | run it in window "watch" of the agentctl session (created if missing) instead of here; also shows the task counts in the status bar of that session |  |
| `--no-status-line` | with --tmux: leave the status bar of the session alone |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl watch --tmux                  # in window "watch" of the agentctl session
agentctl watch                         # in this terminal
```

## agentctl board

Full-screen overview of the tasks: state, progress, a live preview of the selected window, and keys to switch to it, message, interrupt, pull and close.

```
agentctl board [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--tmux` | open it in window "board" of the agentctl session (created if missing) instead of here |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl board --tmux                  # in window "board" of the agentctl session
agentctl board
```

## agentctl notify-test

Send one test notification and say which channel carried it (terminal-notifier with a click action, or the osascript fallback).

```
agentctl notify-test [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl notify-test
```

## agentctl adopt

Restore the state file of a task whose TASK.md is lost (the report and the window are still there). Agent, model and effort default to "unknown".

```
agentctl adopt [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--report <path>` | path of the task report | required |
| `--window <name>` | tmux window of the task (default: the lowercase task ID) |  |
| `--worktree <path>` | worktree of the task, so "close --rm-worktree" knows it |  |
| `--agent <agent>` | agent running in the window | one of `claude`, `codex` |
| `--model <model>` | model of the task |  |
| `--effort <effort>` | effort of the task | one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written, write nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl adopt NC-42 --report ~/Projects/cache/nc-42/NC-42.md --agent claude --worktree ~/Projects/wt/app-nc-42
```

## agentctl interrupt

Interrupt the task's current turn (sends the agent's interrupt key, default Escape); the window stays open.

```
agentctl interrupt [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the command that would run, execute nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl interrupt NC-42
```

## agentctl attach

Go to the task window: attach-session outside tmux, switch-client inside. Without a task: the only running one, or a list to choose from.

```
agentctl attach [options] [task]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[task]` | task ID; case does not matter and a unique prefix is enough |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--switch-client` | for the click on a notification: select the window and switch the tmux client that is attached to the session; never attaches a terminal |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl attach NC-42
agentctl attach nc-4                    # a unique prefix is enough
```

## agentctl event

Called by the agents themselves (hooks that "new" sets up): records the event, updates the task state and notifies at once. Always exits 0.

```
agentctl event [options] [payload]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[payload]` | the event as JSON (codex puts it here; claude sends it on stdin) |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--task <task>` | task ID | required |
| `--agent <agent>` | the agent that reports | one of `claude`, `codex`; required |
| `--kind <kind>` | claude: which hook called | one of `notification`, `stop`, `stop-failure` |
| `--forward <json>` | codex: JSON list, the notify command the user had; run with the same JSON after this one |  |

## agentctl move

Hand a task that hit its usage limit to the other provider: new window \<task>-2 in the same worktree, the original prompt plus a note to continue. Asks y/N.

```
agentctl move [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent <agent>` | move to this provider (default: the other one) | one of `claude`, `codex` |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl move NC-42                    # to the other provider, asks y/N
agentctl move NC-42 --agent codex -y
```

## agentctl peek

Print the last lines of the task window (without the agent footer), to read along without attaching.

```
agentctl peek [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; case does not matter and a unique prefix is enough |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `-n, --lines <n>` | number of lines | default `40` |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl peek NC-42
agentctl peek NC-42 -n 80
```

## agentctl mcp

Local MCP server on stdio: lets a chat (the Claude app, Claude Code, VS Code) read status, window previews and reports. "mcp install" registers it; writing is off until mcp.allow says otherwise.

Subcommands: `mcp serve`, `mcp install`, `mcp uninstall`. Without a subcommand: `serve`.

```
agentctl mcp [options] [command]
```

## agentctl mcp serve

Serve the tools on stdin/stdout (this is what the app or Claude Code starts). Nothing else is ever printed to stdout.

```
agentctl mcp serve [options]
```

## agentctl mcp install

Register this agentctl as an MCP server: --desktop edits claude_desktop_config.json (diff, y/N, dated .bak copy, other servers kept), --claude-code runs "claude mcp add --scope user".

```
agentctl mcp install [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--desktop` | the Claude desktop app |  |
| `--claude-code` | Claude Code (user scope; the VS Code extension reads the same configuration) |  |
| `--config <file>` | with --desktop: use this file instead of ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (to try it on a copy) |  |
| `--dry-run` | show the entry, the diff and the commands; change nothing |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl mcp install --desktop --dry-run
agentctl mcp install --desktop
agentctl mcp install --claude-code
agentctl mcp install --desktop --config ./copy.json --dry-run
```

## agentctl mcp uninstall

Remove the agentctl MCP server from the Claude desktop config and/or Claude Code (without a flag: both).

```
agentctl mcp uninstall [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--desktop` | the Claude desktop app |  |
| `--claude-code` | Claude Code (user scope; the VS Code extension reads the same configuration) |  |
| `--config <file>` | with --desktop: use this file instead of ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (to try it on a copy) |  |
| `--dry-run` | show the entry, the diff and the commands; change nothing |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl mcp uninstall                 # both
agentctl mcp uninstall --desktop
```
